messages.subject: dplyr: group transform problem
messages.subject_clean: dplyr: group transform problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Thanks for the great work on ddply and dplyr. I'm seeing some strange and inconsistent behavior when applying transforms with ddply and dplyr. For example, I would expect the function ``f`` to subtract the group-wise maximum from every value in that group. Instead, dplyr (0.1.3) subtracts the full-data max to every value in the set. ``ddply`` works as expected.

Any thoughts?

Vincent

library(plyr)
library(dplyr)
df = data.frame('a'=gl(10, 10), 'b'=rnorm(100))

f = function(x) x - max(x)
k = ddply(df, 'a', transform, ddply = f(b))
k$bad = k$b - max(k$b)
k$good = unlist(tapply(df$b, df$a, function(i) i - max(i)))
l = df %.% group_by(b) %.% transform(dplyr = f(b))

res = merge(k, l)

messages.subject_clean: dplyr and Sql server and RODBC
messages.body_plain:
Has anyone taken a stab at implementing a dplyr interface to mssql or RODBC?
Looking at Hadley's recent vignettes,http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dplyr/vignettes/new-sql-backend.html , it seems that with an existing DBI interface it "shouldn't" be too difficult.
For mssql we have rsqlserver, a very recent package.
For RODBC we could maybe use RJDBC (which is dbi) and then a JDBC ODBC bridge.
Of course, we could also implement a dbi interface to RODBC, but I somehow doubt that it would be easier.

Any thoughts or any ongoing attempts? I would be happy to collaborate.

messages.subject_clean: Getting coefficients from models fit with dplyr do()
messages.body_plain:
On occasion, I've used plyr to fit multiple models, and extract their coefficients like so.

> library(plyr)
>
> models_plyr <- dlply(mtcars, .(cyl), with, lm(mpg ~ wt))
> coefs_plyr <- ldply(models_plyr, coef)

> #   cyl (Intercept)        wt
> # 1   4    39.57120 -5.647025
> # 2   6    28.40884 -2.780106
> # 3   8    23.86803 -2.192438

I'm curious whether there's a roughly equivalent way in dplyr 0.2.

> library(dplyr)
>
> models_dplyr <- mtcars %>% group_by(cyl)

Here are my attempts, and how they've failed.

> coefs_dplyr <- models_dplyr %>% do(coef(lm))
> # Error: object of type 'closure' is not subsettable

> coefs_dplyr <- models_dplyr %>% coef(.$lm)
> is.null(coefs_dplyr)
> # [1] TRUE

> coefs_dplyr <- models_dplyr %>% summarise(coefs = coef(lm))
> # R encountered a fatal error (in RStudio)

> coefs_dplyr <- models_dplyr %>% ddply(., .(cyl), with, coef(lm))
> # data frame with 0 columns and 0 rows

-Joe

messages.subject: dlply, dropping columns, equivalence classes, and other good stuff
messages.subject_clean: dlply, dropping columns, equivalence classes, and other good stuff
messages.body_plain:
It might be nice to have an option for dropping the columns by which you're splitting.

Currently, I can do that using something like this:

Define example:

xx <- data.frame(a=LETTERS[1:8],b=rep(1:2,each=1),c=rep(1:2,each=2),d=rep(1:2,each=4))

For one variable:

> dlply(xx,.(b),function(q){q[,"b"]<-NULL;q})
$`1`
  a c d
1 A 1 1
2 C 2 1
3 E 1 2
4 G 2 2

$`2`
  a c d
1 B 1 1
2 D 2 1
3 F 1 2
4 H 2 2

attr(,"split_type")
[1] "data.frame"
attr(,"split_labels")
  b
1 1
2 2

For n variables, a little messier:

> vars <- c("b","d")
> dlply(xx,vars,function(q){q[,vars]<-rep(list(NULL),length(vars));q})})
$`1.1`
  a c
1 A 1
2 C 2

$`1.2`
  a c
1 E 1
2 G 2

$`2.1`
  a c
1 B 1
2 D 2

$`2.2`
  a c
1 F 1
2 H 2

attr(,"split_type")
[1] "data.frame"
attr(,"split_labels")
  b d
1 1 1
2 1 2
3 2 1
4 2 2

But this seems pretty clumsy. How about something like dlply(xx,vars,..., .coldrop=TRUE) ?

The motivation for this case was that I was splitting up a data frame by each different column, and then wanted to divide the resulting subframes into equivalence classes to see the mapping from variables to number of equivalence classes:

> xx <- data.frame(a=rep(LETTERS[1:4],2),
                   b=rep(1:2,each=1),
                   c=rep(1:2,each=2),
                   d=rep(1:2,each=4))
> llply(names(xx),
        function(col) { z <- dlply(xx,col,
                                   function (q) { q[,col]<-NULL ; q });
                        match(z,unique(z))
                      }
)

[[1]]           <<< I'd like this to be labelled 'a'
[1] 1 2 3 4     <<< 4 equivalence classes

[[2]]
[1] 1 2

[[3]]
[1] 1 2

[[4]]
[1] 1 1          <<< down to 1

Of course, if people have better suggestions on how to do this (the equivalence classes), I'd be interested.

Also, why doesn't llply have the same names/attributes as dlply, namely attr(,"split_labels")?

For that matter, how can I name the list elements? Do I have to explicitly do zzz <- llply(...); names(zzz) <- names(xx) ) ?

          -s

messages.body_plain:
I've encountered a situation with dplyr where it appears using collect() doesn't sever the umbilical cord to the database you originally query from.

I was previously loading data from a csv file with fread and converting it to a tbl_df, then applying group_by and applying do().

E.g.,

## Get Data
data <- tbl_dt(fread(file))
## group and operate on data
data <- data %.%
    filter((region %in% regions)) %.%
    mutate(time = as.POSIXct(time), type = make.names(paste(region, type))) %.%
    group_by(date, type) %.% do(head(., 1)) %.%
    ungroup() %.% select(date, type, time)

Then I tried to convert my process to querying data from a centralized postgres database and uploaded by data there.

I created my database connection here:

## Get Data
    tmp <- src_postgres(dbname = "postgres", user = "postgres", password = "xxxxx")
    data_postgres <- tbl(tmp, "data")
    c1 <- select(data_postgres, time, date, region, type)
    data <- collect(c1)
## group and operate on data
data <- data %.%
    filter((region %in% regions)) %.%
    mutate(time = as.POSIXct(time), type = make.names(paste(region, type))) %.%
    group_by(date, type) %.% do(head(., 1)) %.%
    ungroup() %.% select(date, type, time)

This appeared to bring in the table from the database and put it in a local data.frame in R memory.

However, when I subsequently went on to the grouping operations it would show a progress bar and what previously was instantaneous in memory, would take a minute, and would show an output of time spent like ===Completed after 1 m   . The above operation applying group_by and do to the df read from disk was instantaneous.

Is there anyway to bring data in from the database into a data.frame and continue operating as if you had read it directly from disk?

I also found that do() on collected data from a database wouldn't be able to refer to the column names in the scope anymore, whereas a dataframe created by reading from disk you could.

I can't find evidence that anyone else has struggled with this, so maybe someone can suggest a better workflow? Or should dplyr be OK with this?

Thanks, Jenny
